channel.description: Recent content in metalcore on Loud Legends

item.title: Spiritbox Performs on Jimmy Kimmel Live, Brings Heavy Metal to Mainstream TV; VIDEO
item.description: Spiritbox, one of the fastest-rising bands in the modern metal scene, made their late-night television debut this week on Jimmy Kimmel Live. The Canadian group performed “Soft Spine”, one of their heaviest tracks to date, giving millions of viewers a taste of extreme metal on national broadcast television.

item.title: BRING ME THE HORIZON Teases New Project With Lo-Fi Versions of Their Songs
item.description: Bring Me The Horizon is exploring a different vibe. On Tuesday (8), the British band shared on Instagram that they’ve been working on a new project featuring lo-fi reinterpretations of their songs.

item.title: Ex-Asking Alexandria DENIS STOFF Reacts To Viral Warped Tour Backlash: 'I Laughed My Tits Off'
item.description: Former Asking Alexandria frontman Denis Stoff has spoken out about recent criticism aimed at current vocalist Danny Worsnop, following a performance that disappointed many fans. The band’s June 15 livestream at the Vans Warped Tour in Washington, D.

item.title: ASKING ALEXANDRIA Responds to Criticism With Instagram Post: 'It's Never F-cking Good Enough'
item.description: Asking Alexandria has drawn attention again, this time through a post on their official Instagram. The band shared a video clip of frontman Danny Worsnop performing the song “Things Could Be Different” during their recent Warped Tour appearance in Washington, D.

item.title: Michael Paget Says BULLET FOR MY VALENTINE's New Album Will Feature 'Crazy Tuning'
item.description: Guitarist Michael “Padge” Paget says BULLET FOR MY VALENTINE is exploring new territory on their next studio album, including tunings the band has never used before. The longtime member of the Welsh metalcore group opened up about the upcoming record during a chat at this year’s Download Festival in the UK (watch the interview below).

item.title: ASKING ALEXANDRIA Fans Question Danny Worsnop’s Performance, Call for His Exit
item.description: Asking Alexandria’s recent Warped Tour performance is stirring debate online, and some fans think it may be time for lead singer Danny Worsnop to step aside. The band’s subreddit lit up after their June 15 set, with over a dozen posts and hundreds of comments discussing Worsnop’s vocals and stage presence.

item.title: BULLET FOR MY VALENTINE's Michael Paget On New Album: 'It's Gonna Be Super Heavy'
item.description: BULLET FOR MY VALENTINE is working on new music, and according to guitarist Michael “Padge” Paget, fans should expect something heavier than ever before. The Welsh metal band recently cut its joint tour with Trivium short, choosing to focus instead on writing and recording their next studio album.

item.title: FIT FOR A KING Announces New Album 'LONELY GOD', Shares Lead Single And Tracklist
item.description: Fit For A King have unveiled Lonely God, their eighth studio album, scheduled to arrive August 1, 2025 via Solid State Records. The announcement came with a music video (available at the end of this article) for the blistering title track, which showcases the band’s signature blend of gnarly riffs, guttural growls, heavy grooves, and a dash of industrial crunch.

item.title: JESSE LEACH Talks About KILLSWITCH ENGAGE's 'Aftermath': 'We All Have a Responsibility'
item.description: Killswitch Engage isn’t wasting time with metaphors or feel-good slogans in their latest single. The video for “Aftermath” just dropped, and it doesn’t sugarcoat a thing. If you were expecting a fun, breakdown-heavy anthem about “staying strong,” keep scrolling.

item.title: MATT TUCK Says BULLET FOR MY VALENTINE Will Return To Studio: 'We Can't Wait To Drop New Music'
item.description: While stomping around Donington Park for the Download Festival in the UK, Matt Tuck finally offered something resembling an update on Bullet For My Valentine’s elusive eighth studio album.

item.title: Mike Portnoy Surprises Son Max With Dream Theater Drum Challenge at Drumeo
item.description: Max Portnoy walked into Drumeo expecting a normal day. Instead, his father, Mike Portnoy, waited for him with a surprise. Mike asked his son to play Honor Thy Father by Dream Theater without any practice.

item.title: KILLSWITCH ENGAGE Shares Music Video For 'Collusion' Single From 'This Consequence' Album
item.description: Killswitch Engage is back with This Consequence, their ninth studio album, and they’ve just unleashed a music video for the track “Collusion”, which, spoiler alert, is NOT about happy things.

item.title: Killswitch Engage’s Mike D’Antonio Rejects A.I. Claims: "I Don’t Wanna Be Associated With It"
item.description: Another day, another internet conspiracy theory—this time, aimed at Killswitch Engage bassist and graphic designer Mike D’Antonio, who’s had to crawl out of the art cave he’s been living in for the past eight months just to tell people to shut the hell up about A.

item.title: The Callous Daoboys Announce New Album "I Don’t Want to See You in Heaven"
item.description: Let me set the scene for ya: It’s 2 AM, I’ve had too much coffee, and I’m staring at my laptop like it owes me money. Somewhere in Atlanta, The Callous Daoboys are probably plotting their next auditory crime, gearing up to unleash I Don’t Want to See You in Heaven on May 16 via MNRK Heavy.

item.title: Heidi Shepherd Speaks Out on Vocal Training: “I Was a Singer Before I Was a Screamer”
item.description: Apparently some people still think Heidi Shepherd—frontwoman of BUTCHER BABIES, growler of unholy things, destroyer of vocal cords (except, not hers, more on that later)—can’t sing. And she’s had enough.

item.title: Stray From The Path Releases “Kubrick Stare” – A New Single Under SharpTone Records; VIDEO
item.description: Stray From The Path is back. And they’re bringing paranoia with them. Their latest single, “Kubrick Stare”, just dropped (February 5, 2025, mark it) with a music video that’s—well, unsettling, in the best way.

item.title: My Ticket Home to Play First Show Since 2018—Here’s What to Expect
item.description: Let’s be real. Band reunions? They happen. All. The. Time. Some of them feel like a warm, nostalgic hug. Others? Like a desperate cash grab at the last scraps of remember-us-please energy.

item.title: As I Lay Dying: Tim Lambesis Accuses Ex-Wife of Physical and Mental Abuse
item.description: The ongoing implosion of As I Lay Dying feels less like a band breakup and more like a reality show nobody asked for. The last few months have been a cascade of exits, with band members dropping out faster than you can say “personal integrity.

item.title: Tim Lambesis Faces Solo Challenge as As I Lay Dying Joins Rockville 2025
item.description: The lineup for Welcome to Rockville 2025 has been rolling out steadily, but one name caught more than a few raised eyebrows this weekend—As I Lay Dying. For those not keeping score, the band is now essentially just Tim Lambesis.

item.title: Welcome to Rockville 2025 Books As I Lay Dying Despite Chaos
item.description: The wreckage that is 2024 As I Lay Dying looks more like a construction zone than a band these days, but apparently, that’s not stopping Tim Lambesis from slapping the name on a festival poster.

item.title: Tim Lambesis to Continue As I Lay Dying After Major Band Departures
item.description: Tim Lambesis seems hell-bent on keeping As I Lay Dying alive, despite the complete meltdown the band’s endured recently. Over the past few weeks, total chaos erupted as band members exited left and right without a word from Lambesis, until now.

item.title: Phil Sgrosso Joins Mass Departure from As I Lay Dying; See Details
item.description: Phil Sgrosso has left As I Lay Dying behind, joining the recent exodus from a band that now stands with only Tim Lambesis on board. After nearly two decades of dedication split across two stints—2003 to 2014, and again from 2018 to now—Sgrosso decided it was time to step back.

item.title: As I Lay Dying's Comeback Album Mysteriously Disappears From Streaming
item.description: Mysterious times for As I Lay Dying fans. The band’s 2019 comeback album, Shaped By Fire, has all but vanished from streaming platforms, and the silence around its absence just adds to the mystery.

item.title: Band Exodus: As I Lay Dying Loses Three Members in One Week
item.description: The slow-motion collapse of what’s left of As I Lay Dying keeps unraveling. It began with bassist and clean vocalist Ryan Neff deciding to call it quits earlier this week.

item.title: As I Lay Dying: Tim Lambesis’ Wife Denies Abuse Claims as Band Falls Apart
item.description: The ongoing collapse of As I Lay Dying is starting to look like the band’s final encore. Over the past week, three members and their manager have jumped ship.

item.title: KEN SUSI Walks Away from AS I LAY DYING: "My Morals Hit Their Limit"
item.description: The As I Lay Dying ship seems to be taking on water—fast. First, bassist Ryan Neff jumped overboard, offering little more than a vague farewell. Then whispers started about their European tour vanishing into thin air, allegedly after their tour manager quit.

item.title: Drummer Nick Pierce Leaves As I Lay Dying Citing Health Concerns
item.description: As I Lay Dying seems to be unraveling faster than a cheap sweater at a metal merch stand. The band now consists of just Tim Lambesis and Phil Sgrosso, as drummer Nick Pierce becomes the latest member to exit stage left.

item.title: European Tour Canceled as As I Lay Dying Faces Major Member Departures
item.description: It’s a mass exodus over in the As I Lay Dying camp, with members dropping off faster than you can say “farewell tour.” The band’s entire European tour is scrapped, and not a peep has come from the remaining members—whoever’s still sticking around, that is.

item.title: Ryan Neff Exits As I Lay Dying: Another Chapter in the Band’s Soap Opera
item.description: Bassist and vocalist Ryan Neff decided his time with As I Lay Dying was short-lived, officially announcing his departure on October 18. The timing? Right before the band gears up for a sprawling European tour.

item.title: Ice Nine Kills Drummer Patrick Galante Steps Down
item.description: Ice Nine Kills just lost a piece of their rhythm section, and no, it’s not some dramatic ‘spooky’ horror movie twist. Patrick Galante, who’s been holding down the drum kit since 2018, has decided to hang up his sticks—at least with INK.

item.title: As I Lay Dying Previews 'Through Storms Ahead' With New Single; VIDEO
item.description: As I Lay Dying has rolled out their latest offering, “Whitewashed Tomb,” a mid-tempo track that gives a preview of their upcoming album, Through Storms Ahead, slated for release on November 15.

item.title: As I Lay Dying: 'We Are The Dead' Drops with Alex Terrible and Tom Barber; VIDEO
item.description: As I Lay Dying is gearing up to drop their latest album, Through Storms Ahead, set to land on November 15. Nestled among the tracks are “Burden,” “The Cave We Fear to Enter,” and the freshly unleashed “We Are The Dead.

item.title: AS I LAY DYING Announces Eighth Album 'Through Storms Ahead'
item.description: Two and a half decades and a pile of albums later, AS I LAY DYING is tossing another entry onto their discography stack. Their eighth studio album, “Through Storms Ahead”, hits shelves (or playlists, let’s be honest) on November 15, 2024, courtesy of Napalm Records.

item.title: Phil Labonte: Korn’s Impact on Deathcore Goes Beyond Nu-Metal
item.description: When a band ends up becoming so influential that people start crediting them for launching a whole subgenre, it’s something to take note of. But when a group gets blamed for a genre they don’t even directly belong to?

item.title: As I Lay Dying Drops Emotional New Track, "The Cave We Fear to Enter"; VIDEO
item.description: Looks like As I Lay Dying has decided to venture into metaphorical spelunking. Their latest single, “The Cave We Fear to Enter,” leans heavily into clean vocals and was born out of an idea from bassist and vocalist Ryan Neff.

item.title: AS I LAY DYING and Jordan Mancino Part Ways: Legal Drama and New Drummer Nick Pierce
item.description: Jordan Mancino, the drummer who had been with As I Lay Dying since the early days, seems to have permanently checked out. Not in a quiet, amicable way either—this one comes with lawyers, statements, and all the usual mess you’d expect when band relationships implode.

item.title: Watch: As I Lay Dying Is Back: 'Burden' Released, Tour Announced
item.description: As I Lay Dying has returned with “Burden”, their first new single in five years, featuring their revamped lineup. The track introduces Ken Susi (ex-Unearth), Nick Pierce (ex-Unearth), and Ryan Neff (Miss May I), marking a new chapter for the band.

item.title: AS I LAY DYING’s New Album Delayed: Tim Lambesis Explains Why
item.description: Tim Lambesis, AS I LAY DYING’s frontman, recently chatted on the Loaded Radio podcast about the band’s long-gestating new album. Apparently, the record’s been done for a while, but mixing has turned into a never-ending tug-of-war.

item.title: AS I LAY DYING Finalizes New Record Deal for 2024 Album
item.description: When Tim Lambesis sat down with Jamey Jasta on the “The Jasta Show”, the HATEBREED frontman probably knew he’d get some juicy tidbits on AS I LAY DYING’s new material.

item.title: AS I LAY DYING Delays Album Completion Again; See Details
item.description: Here we are again, AS I LAY DYING has a new album brewing, but don’t hold your breath just yet. Vocalist Tim Lambesis, in an interview with Chaoszine, dished out the details, or at least as much as anyone could get from his roundabout explanations.

item.title: AS I LAY DYING's Tim Lambesis on New Album: “As Passionate as Ever”
item.description: Tim Lambesis, the ever-controversial voice behind AS I LAY DYING, let slip in a recent chat with the Today’s Boondoggle podcast that the band’s next studio album is set to land later this year (2024).

item.title: As I Lay Dying Begins Recording New Album With Fresh Lineup
item.description: The wheels are turning again for As I Lay Dying, and Tim Lambesis, the band’s infamous frontman, has confirmed their new album is officially in progress. Speaking with Heavy New York, Lambesis revealed that the group’s latest lineup is pulling its weight in the studio.

item.title: As I Lay Dying Recruits Nick Pierce as Drummer for Tour; See Details
item.description: Jordan Mancino, the drummer who’s been part of As I Lay Dying since the beginning, has decided to step away from the band’s upcoming Two Decades of Destruction Tour.

item.title: Jordan Mancino Steps Back: As I Lay Dying Faces Internal Challenges
item.description: The chaos surrounding As I Lay Dying just keeps piling up. After Josh Gilbert made his grand exit, the band scrambled to patch things together by roping in Ryan Neff of Miss May I to cover bass and vocals, while Ken Susi of Unearth stepped in on guitar.
